mp2:0.1: Worshipping the Virtues of the Three Treasures
mp2:1.1: Worshipping the Virtues of the Buddha
mp2:2.1: Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha,
mp2:2.2: the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the one who understands the worlds,
mp2:2.3: the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming,
mp2:2.4: the Teacher of gods and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One.
mp2:3.1: Worshipping the Virtues of the Dhamma
mp2:4.1: The Dhamma has been well-proclaimed by the Fortunate One, it is visible, not subject to time,
mp2:4.2: inviting inspection, onward leading, and can be understood by the wise for themselves.
mp2:5.1: Worshipping the Virtues of the Saṅgha
mp2:6.1: The Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are good in their practice,
mp2:6.2: the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are upright in their practice,
mp2:6.3: the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are systematic in their practice,
mp2:6.4: the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples are correct in their practice,
mp2:6.5: that is to say, the four pairs of persons, the eight individual persons,
mp2:6.6: this is the Fortunate One’s Saṅgha of disciples,
mp2:6.7: they are worthy of offerings, of hospitality, of gifts, and of reverential salutation,
mp2:6.8: they are an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.
mp2:8.1: By this declaration of the truth may the three treasures appear to you!
mp2:9.1: By this declaration of the truth may the three treasures appear to you!
mp2:10.1: By this declaration of the truth may the three treasures appear to you!
